definition.description: Lie supine with both knees bent and feet supported on the floor. Raise the hips through a comfortable active range, then lower and reset under control. One repetition is one bilateral floor-supported hip rise and return. This excludes Hip Thrust, bridge march, walkout, single-leg bridge, static hold, loaded floor bridge, testing, and forced end range.

environment.space: room to lie, bridge, and exit safely
environment.changeRule: Changing upper-body support, laterality, load, range, foot position, pause, tempo, dose, surface, or intent requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: can use the supine floor base and exit safely
can perform a small bilateral active hip rise without symptom escalation
session logistics and downstream demands fit
excludeOrEscalate: symptom, restriction, unsafe supine base, surface, or communication conflict
sharp, increasing, unfamiliar, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or communication concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal foot position, hip height, dose, recovery, outcome, readiness threshold, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 64 reassessed with explicit floor-support boundary from Hip Thrust and exact alternate boundaries.

anatomy.claimsBoundary: Task mechanics only; no diagnosis, treatment, injury-prevention, or performance claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate low-load floor hip-extension work only when the exact base, range, and dose fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Press through both feet, lift from the hips without arching your back, then lower slowly.
secondaryCues: make the range smaller before forcing height
stop before pain or persistent cramping
expectedSensations: possible hamstring effort without persistent cramp
unexpectedSensations: pain, numbness, tingling, dizziness, persistent cramp, or a back-driven lift
selfChecks: hips rise and lower under control
trunk does not create the range

observationChecklist: active hip rise and controlled return
range, cadence, cramp, symptoms, and first quality loss

faultCorrections.lumbar_extension: reduce range and restore trunk organisation
faultCorrections.persistent_hamstring_cramp: adjust foot position or range, rest, or stop
faultCorrections.loss_of_bilateral_support: return to the exact bilateral baseline or revalidate another task

doNotUseWhen: the surface, supine base, exit route, or communication is unsafe
the task conflicts with symptoms or restrictions
the intended task is Hip Thrust, march, walkout, single-leg, static, loaded, testing, or forced range

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop unresolved safety, symptom, base, or quality issues.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any task change reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, substitutions, and validation.

sourceVariant.archiveReason: The source lacks exact cycle, range/support, fatigue, delivery, alternate, calibration, and review contracts.

requirements.cycleRule: one active hip rise to a comfortable controlled top position and return is one repetition
requirements.rangeRule: comfortable active hip extension without back-driven range, pain, or persistent cramp

dosage.countRule: count only controlled bilateral floor rise-return repetitions without pain, persistent cramp, or back-driven range

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: The floor-supported bilateral base, foot contact, trunk, hip rise, return, and breath remain controlled; range is comfortable; and no stop symptom appears.
stopRules: stop on pain, new symptoms, dizziness, persistent cramp, unsafe surface, or participant request
stop when foot contact, trunk, range, or controlled return cannot be restored
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Set the floor base and foot position, observe pelvis and trunk, reduce range before adding volume, and revalidate any support/laterality/load change.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Set both feet, press through the floor, lift your hips without arching, lower slowly, and stop before pain or persistent cramping.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate preparation only; no outcome is guaranteed.

doseScaling.reduce: smaller range, fewer repetitions, slower cadence, padding, more rest, or another reviewed task
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add upper-back support, unilateral load, marching, walkout, external load, or long holds without revalidation.

supportPrompts.athlete: Both feet down; hips lift; ribs stay quiet.
supportPrompts.coach: Floor support is an identity boundary, not an athlete-skill label.

legacy.description: Archived Source 64 remains traceable as an underspecified Glute Bridge skeleton.
legacy.loadNote: Candidate-only; use the exact floor-supported bilateral base and record range, foot position, compensation, cramp, and symptoms.
legacy.cardSummary: Source 64 is represented by an exact candidate contract rather than its vague legacy row.
legacy.coachLanguage: Use an exact candidate only after base, range, duration, fatigue, and downstream-demand checks.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Both feet down; lift from your hips and lower with control.

coachingExecution.quality_gate: Legacy source is not selectable; use exact candidate contract.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact floor base, bilateral support, range, controlled rise/return, symptoms, communication, dose, and downstream task—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: confirm stable floor/mat and exit route
confirm a small controlled bilateral rise and return
confirm stop signal and clear space
stopSigns: dizziness, chest, neurologic, circulation, balance, or support symptoms
persistent cramp, forced range, or persistent quality loss
contraindications: Hip Thrust, march, walkout, single-leg, static, loaded, testing, or forced-range intent
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after revalidation.
Do not treat Hip Thrust, bridge march/walkout, single-leg bridge, static hold, or loaded bridge as automatic substitutions.

score.reviewNotes: Candidate task-only reassessment; independent calibration required.

difficultyProfile.notes: Exact bodyweight bilateral floor Glute Bridge only.
